dialogue.line: This is your breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We've done harder.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'm ready to go.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, how's the cold?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Better. Ready to work.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Better than me, probably.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Drink the tea. Both of you.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One day. Then we winterize. But first we finish.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can work the whole day.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: I'm counting on that.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'll keep up.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You two on beams, Finn and Bear moving materials?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Exactly.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Even if I drop things?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You won't drop them today.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Drink up. We need to move.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: One roof. One day.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Let's earn it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Let's earn it.

action: Eats quickly despite his fever, checking on Finn between bites, then stands ready to head back to the build site.
thought: Eight hours of work. Then we're weatherproof.

action: Manages the thin lunch, making sure everyone eats and gets water from the bucket, then stands at the porch edge watching her family.
thought: They'll hold till nightfall. They have to.

action: Eats quickly, asks about the afternoon plan, nods when Cole entrusts the west side to him, feeling the weight and pride of real responsibility.
thought: He's counting on me. I can lead this.

action: Eats what he can despite nausea, restless and frustrated at being held back from the work, but quiet and trusting his dad's judgment.
thought: Just one more day. I can rest.

action: Eats his portion, makes jokes to lighten the mood, understands his job is morale and supplies, and tags along to the build site ready to help.
thought: I'm helping. I'm part of this.

description: A thin lunch at the porch on the final day: Cole and Sawyer brace for the afternoon push, Finn fights sickness and restlessness, Bear jokes despite hunger, and Maggie holds them all to the finish line.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Quick lunch, everyone. Eat what you can.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is it... more than yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It's what we have, bear. Make it count.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: How you holding up, buddy?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'm fine. Can we work after?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You rest today. Doctor's orders.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Your mom's right. One afternoon push, then we're done.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The roof's so close, though.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Couple hours of solid work. That's all we need.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Then we can build the walls, right?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Then we winterize. One thing at a time, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: At least the sun's still here.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: This roof before the cold comes. That's the whole game.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You've got the right idea. Lead the west side this afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yeah. I can do that.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I help?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You hand up supplies. Keep morale alive. That's your job.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I should be up there.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, I need you sharp for winter. Rest now.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: At least we're not hungry for long—we'll be too tired to eat.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Bear, that's not the encouragement I was aiming for.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How much of the day do we have left?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good eight hours of light. More than enough.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Then finish your food and get back there.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Tonight we'll have a roof over us for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: A real roof. Not the tarp.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the thought. Let's hold it.

action: On the roof with Sawyer, Cole secures the final shingles while fighting off a cough, pausing only to check each seam before they move to the next.
thought: One more section and we're home.

action: Maggie stands at the porch with the water jug, watching the boys work and timing the final push, ready to call them in when the light starts to fail.
thought: One more day. We can hold.

action: Sawyer mirrors Cole's work, driving nails with steady focus, his young shoulders squared against the weight of finishing what they started.
thought: I won't let Dad down today.

action: Finn sits below the roof staging materials and shingles up to Cole and Sawyer, coughing but moving steadily, refusing to sit out the final afternoon.
thought: Staying till it's done, no matter what.

action: Bear scurries across the yard gathering fallen scraps and keeping the work area clear, hungry and chattering about the roof nearly being done.
thought: The roof is almost finished! Almost!

description: On the final afternoon, Cole and Sawyer race the roof while Finn stages shingles despite a cough, Bear ferries scraps, and Maggie watches from the porch. One day left.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One more section, Sawyer. We've got this.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The corners are holding. We're close.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Bundle's ready. Take your time, I'm good.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: When do we eat? I'm so hungry.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After we finish, buddy. One more push.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Bear, grab those fallen shingles by the sawhorse.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Already did! The pile's super clean.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Dad, this seam—should I double-seal it?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good eye. Yeah. Make it tight.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: You guys are so close. I can feel it.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Water, everybody. Drink while you're moving.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Smart. Sawyer, drink with me. Two minutes.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The roof is almost done! The roof is almost done!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It is, sweetheart. Your brothers are finishing it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Last bundle coming up. You ready?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Ready. Hand it here.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, sit down if you need to. No heroics.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'm fine. I want to see it done.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I nail something? Anything?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Not today, buddy. But you're doing great.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Thirty minutes of good light left. You've got it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Last corner. Dad, we're almost done.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Almost done. That's right.

action: Hangs the last shingle as the light fades, then walks the porch railing to check the seals one final time before settling on the steps.
thought: Roof's tight. We made it through.

action: Dishes a thin but steaming stew into bowls on the porch bench, using the last of the stock and the fish Sawyer pulled from the creek this morning.
thought: Enough to hold. Enough to be home.

action: Sets down his hammer in the toolbox and joins Cole on the porch steps, shoulders loose with a quiet sense of done.
thought: I didn't let him down today.

action: Coughs twice, then curls up on a log bench by the stove's warmth, watching everyone settle and feeling the day finally leave his bones.
thought: Finally done. I can finally rest.

action: Plops down on the porch floor next to Maggie's bench, swinging his legs happily despite his hunger, excited to eat and to be still.
thought: We finished it! The roof is done!

description: The roof is sealed; dusk settles on Day Nine. Cole and Sawyer rest on the porch steps while Maggie dishes a thin but steaming stew, Finn curls by the stove's glow, and Bear sits close, all of them quiet with exhaustion but whole.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Roof is done! We're weatherproof, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: All sealed. Winter won't find a gap in this one.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Stew's ready. Come and eat while it's warm.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How much longer till we can sleep?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Eat, rest. That's all for tonight.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: My hands are done. My whole self is done.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: But we DID it. We actually did it.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You did. All of you. I saw it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How are you feeling, Dad?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Tired, sick, and proud. Three out of three.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I eat in here by the fire?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Yes. Bring your bowl inside.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Tomorrow we build the walls, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We do. But tonight, we rest and eat.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The cabin's actually going to be a real house.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It already is. You made it one.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: This stew tastes better than anything I've eaten.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Because we earned it!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Because your mom made it with love.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And because you all worked until the light ran out.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We should sleep before anything breaks.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Already fixed. Now we eat, then the cabin.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we stay up just a little?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat first. Then we'll see.

action: Rests on the porch steps with a warm bowl, watching the cabin glow and listening to the family settle.
thought: The roof will hold. We made it.

action: Carries a small pot of reheated stew to the porch, checking each of her sick boys as she moves.
thought: Three down with cough. I'll keep them warm tonight.

action: Sits on the porch with his bowl, eating slowly, too tired to move much.
thought: The roof is done. Dad's proud of me.

action: Rests on blankets inside the cabin near the warm stove, coughing quietly, finally still.
thought: So tired. The roof is finished. Done.

action: Sits close to Maggie on the porch, eating his share and bouncing with tired pride about the finished roof.
thought: We did it. The roof is real.

description: With the roof sealed tight, the family settles on the porch and around the warm cabin—three boys heavy-eyed with cough, Maggie moving between them with quiet care.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Everyone gets a bowl. Even you, Sawyer.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I'm okay, Mom. I can eat.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: I know. You're all okay. That's the miracle.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn's resting inside. Good call.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: But the roof! We actually finished it!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We did. Because of you too, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Really? I was just running around.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: You kept the scraps moving. That's the job.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat while it's warm. Tomorrow's a new day.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: A day without hammers on my head, at least.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: What are we building next?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Walls, probably. Before winter comes.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: First we rest. And eat more. Food's too low.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Town run's due Monday maybe.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I come?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Depends on who's still coughing.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can help with the next build.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: I know you can. But tonight, just rest.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: My cough's not so bad!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat your stew, Bear.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: But we're gonna build walls, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Walls, a real door, maybe some windows.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: —from inside— Did someone say windows?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Finn, rest. You're still fighting that cough.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Light'll pour in. Maggie can choose where.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That'll make it feel more like a home.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It's already a home. But I like where you're headed.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can windows have a view of the moose?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: If the moose cooperates, sure.

action: Stokes the fire and surveys the day—the roof held overnight, and there's the woodshed to plan.
thought: Roof held. Now the real work begins.

action: Dishes eggs and checks on the three boys, wrapping Sawyer in a warmed shirt against the cough.
thought: Boys are healing. We've earned this rest.

action: Eats slowly, chest sore from coughing, but helps stack breakfast plates with quiet pride in the roof.
thought: Chest aches, but the roof is solid.

action: Bounces on the porch steps, restless with energy, asking what's next before breakfast is even cleared.
thought: So much to build. Can't wait to start.

action: Huddles by the stove, coughing but smiling, watching everyone move and warming his small hands on the hot mug.
thought: Warm cabin, my family, and the day.

description: Morning warmth: stove crackles, roof held overnight, three boys coughing but healing, and Cole's already eyeing the woodshed while Maggie dishes eggs.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Coffee's hot. Sleep okay?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: All three still coughing, but warm enough.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: My chest is sore from coughing, not the work.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: What's the plan today? Woodshed?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One step at a time, bud.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm ready to help! I'm strong now!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat first, hero. You need the fuel.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Roof held overnight. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It did. Team effort.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we start framing the shed today?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: School first. Then we'll see.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we do math by the fire?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Maybe. Finish your eggs.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can work light today. Stack wood?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Yeah. Easy pace. No rushing.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: School is so slow right now.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It keeps your brain sharp.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: My brain is plenty sharp. I knew the roof would hold!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That was the four of us who built it, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Sawyer, drink something warm for that cough.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I'm okay. Really.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: I know. But humor me.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: So when does the woodshed actually start?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Today, if we finish clearing the site.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The woodshed! The big one by the creek?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the plan.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One day at a time, team.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We can do it. Roof's already proof.

action: After confirming the roof held overnight, Cole walks the woodshed site and gathers the boys to assess it before lunch.
thought: The roof held. Now shoring up before winter.

action: Maggie wraps the morning lessons at the porch table, sets out bread and cheese for lunch, and watches Cole return with the boys from the site.
thought: School done, boys healing, the rhythm is working.

action: Sawyer coughs through the last problem, then eagerly follows Cole and his brothers out to the woodshed site, chest aching but pride warming him.
thought: Dad sees the roof work I did. That matters.

action: Finn bounces through the last math problem and races out to the site with Cole and Sawyer, already tumbling with ideas about framing.
thought: Building again! There's so much we can make.

action: Bear finishes his lesson early and darts ahead toward the woodshed site, coughing but first to scope the salvage wood and open space.
thought: I can help build! I'm the wood finder.

description: Maggie calls the boys to lunch at the porch as Cole returns from checking the woodshed site, three recovering kids at his heels, already eager about the next big build.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One more problem, Finn, then you're done.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can't we just skip math and build?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's not how it works, bud.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Can we look at the woodshed now?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After lessons. You're still healing.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: But I'm feeling better!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One more day. Then we build.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We're allowed to look though, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Looking is free. That's planning.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long for the project?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Three, four days if salvage wood works.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And if it doesn't?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Then we figure it out. We always do.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: There's salvage on the property?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Pallets, fallen logs, all over.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: So we're not buying materials?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Can't afford to right now. We use what we have.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I find the wood?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're naturally good at that.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Let's go look. Maggie's got lunch ready soon.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Let's see this site.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Come on, Bear! Come on!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm right here! I'm coming!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The woodshed goes right here.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That's a big space. How much will it hold?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Six cords of wood, maybe eight.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: That's huge!

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We can build that. Easy.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Three days of work. Four if it rains.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The roof took longer, and that was bigger.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: True. You're ready for this. Let's head back for lunch.

action: Cole directs the woodpile reorganization from the site, pointing out where to clear and how to stack, working alongside Sawyer to move larger logs into a tighter configuration.
thought: The roof held. Now we winterize.

action: Maggie watches from the porch, speaking up when Finn or Bear overreach, keeping the afternoon's rhythm steady while the boys learn what their healing bodies can manage.
thought: Boys are healing. The rhythm works.

action: Sawyer works shoulder-to-shoulder with Cole, hauling the longer logs and asking questions about the next build stage, his chest aching but his mind sharp on the work.
thought: Dad trusts my ideas. That's growth.

action: Finn gathers fallen branches and hands them off to the stacking pile, moving carefully and quietly, pleased to feel his chest hurt less with each gentle exertion.
thought: Helping while healing. I'm getting better.

action: Bear bounces between the woodpile and the yard, finding sticks and fallen wood with his eyes lit up, calling out each discovery like a hunter bringing home the prize.
thought: I'm strong enough to help here!

description: Afternoon light slants across the homestead as Cole directs a full woodpile reorganization—Sawyer hauling larger logs alongside him, Finn and Bear gathering branches with quiet determination—while Maggie watches from the porch, calling out when to rest, and the family moves through the work with the easy rhythm of people who've found their groove.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Easy, you two—still getting your strength back, remember.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: But Mom, I found so much wood already!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Light work is good for them. Listen to your mom.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: If we clear this end, the pile gets way tighter.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's smart thinking. Show me what you mean.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I hand off branches? My arms feel okay.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Perfect, Finn. Passing, not heavy lifting.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: More branches! There's so much wood out here!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Easy, buddy. We're building a system, not racing.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long until the woodshed is full?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Few more days at this pace. But we're getting there.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And look—both boys are stronger already.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: My chest doesn't hurt as bad when I move.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Mine either! I'm getting better!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's what healing looks like. Keep it steady.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Dad, should we ask about shed materials on the next town run?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good thinking. We'll need to. For now, organize this.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Which means rest time is coming up soon.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Aw, come on—

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: No arguing. Dinner's in an hour anyway.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we sit by the stove after, when it's warm?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: If the cough settles down, sure thing.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Let's see how they sound by then.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The roof held through the night. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It did. One big thing locked in. Now we finish the rest.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: And we're helping! All of us helping!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We are, bear. All of us, together.

action: Stands at the fire's edge as dusk settles, checking the sky for aurora and planning the woodshed frame with Sawyer, the roof's success giving him quiet certainty.
thought: The roof held. We're steady.

action: Sets out bowls of stew and dried vegetables on the porch table, then calls the boys to gather while Finn helps carry plates toward the warmth.
thought: Everyone's here, whole, healing together.

action: Joins Cole at the fire, talking through the weatherization plan for the woodshed—measurements, frame pitch, timeline—his tired energy sharpening into focus.
thought: Dad sees the plan in my head.

action: Carries dishes from the porch toward the fire, helping Maggie with an eagerness that shows he's healing fast, then settles close to the warmth with a full belly.
thought: I'm strong again. I can help build.

action: Settles by the fire with his bowl, warming his small frame in the glow and listening to the big talk while eating, his eyes following the smoke toward the darkening sky.
thought: The fire is warm. We're safe here.

description: The roof held through the day, and as evening falls clear and cool, the family gathers at the fire—Maggie bringing food from the porch, Cole and Sawyer planning the next build, and Finn and Bear warming themselves close to the flames.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Alright, boys—dinner's ready. Come to the fire.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is it the stew? I smell stew!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Your mom's been simmering that since noon. Come on.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The roof really held, Dad. I checked the rafters again.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Solid work. Both of you. I'd stake the winter on that join.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Does that mean we're gonna build more stuff?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One thing at a time, Finn. Eat first.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we build a chicken coop? Chickens are cool.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We need to weatherize first. Close up the gaps.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's right. And get the woodshed roof on before the snow.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: How much firewood do we need to feel safe?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Another cord, maybe two. We've got time.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I can split wood! I'm getting strong again.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm the best wood finder. I found that big one.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You did. That oak's solid. Good eye.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Sawyer's been thinking about the shed design, haven't you?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yeah. Simple frame, roof pitch for snow load. We could start tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Materials are tight, but the frame's doable with what we've got.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We have so many branches behind the treeline!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: And Dad's got nails in the truck!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Everyone's thinking like builders. That's how you know it's working.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The roof held because we got it right and worked it solid.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: So tomorrow we measure the shed site?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: First light. You and me.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I come?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll need everyone. You and Bear gather good straight poles.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I use the axe?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: The hatchet, Bear. You're careful, but not that careful yet.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Okay, the hatchet. I'm really careful now.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: I know you are, buddy.

action: Settles beside the fire with a long breath, watching clear stars form in the darkening sky.
thought: The roof held. We're locking it in.

action: Brings warm tea to the fire, settles on the porch bench with Bear tucked against her side.
thought: Everyone's here, safe, and warm. This is enough.

action: Sits near the fire with his knees drawn up, watching the flames and listening to Dad talk.
thought: I helped build something real. Dad saw that.

action: Curls up near the fire, warming his hands and watching embers glow, fighting off sleep.
thought: Tomorrow we finish the north side.

action: Nestles against Maggie's side, warm and mesmerized by the fire's glow and the safe feeling.
thought: Fire's warm. Everyone's happy. I'm safe.

description: After the roof held all day, the family gathers at the clear-night fire, warm and content; Cole and Sawyer stand together while Bear nestles against Maggie, Finn drowsy, watching stars climb.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That clear sky means stars tonight.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Cold tomorrow, I'd guess. Good day to finish what we started.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The roof really held the whole day, didn't it?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Didn't sag an inch. You did solid work, Saw.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Thanks, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I helped too! I carried branches!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You carried the biggest ones, buddy. Don't you forget it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Tomorrow the north side's next, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: If the weather holds. But tonight, we rest.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And eat. Are you all warm?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Warmest place in the world is right here by this fire.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Warmer than the cabin?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Almost. The stove keeps the cabin at a good heat.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We'll seal the leaks next week, Dad said.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One job at a time. Tonight, just be warm and full.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I like full and warm.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Me too.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: So do I, buddy. So do I.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Do you think we'll finish before the real cold comes?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One more week like today? We lock it in.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And if the weather shifts, we adapt. That's what we do.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That's true.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm getting sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's the day catching up with you. Sleep comes easy when you've earned it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we stay out a little longer?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Soon as you finish your tea.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The stars are coming out.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can see Polaris from here.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good eyes, son. You know what that means.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We're true north. Home.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's exactly right.

action: Settles warm by the fire for breakfast after checking the cabin's corners, finding no water damage anywhere in the clear morning light.
thought: The roof held strong through the night.

action: Stokes the stove and brings warm bread and smoked fish to the fire, calling everyone to gather and eat.
thought: Everyone's fed, safe, here with me.

action: Eats breakfast with Cole, talking about taking a lighter day and walking the north fence line slowly after the roof work.
thought: Yesterday's work was real and honest.

action: Bounces between the fire and the cabin front, eating quickly while asking about fishing and what the day holds.
thought: Can we fish? Please, can we fish?

action: Stays close to Maggie while eating, warm and drowsy, content to listen to the adults while the fire crackles.
thought: Warm food, warm stove, everyone here.

description: The roof held through the clear night with no leaks; the family gathers warm by the stove and fire for breakfast, slow and easy together.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Stove's warm. Come eat, everyone—bread's fresh.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: No leaks in the north corner. Roof held beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Even with the frost last night?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Especially with the frost. Good work yesterday, son.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we fish today instead of building?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I want to see if there's snow up high.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat first, boys—you need fuel for anything.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: After yesterday's push, I'm thinking we take it slower.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Just maintenance and checks?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Maintenance, walk the perimeter, maybe some wood. Nothing heavy.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Rest earned, I'd say.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Does the roof rest too?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Roofs don't rest, Bear.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: But this one's earned a quiet day.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We could walk the north fence line.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good idea. But take your time—no rush today.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: More bread, Finn?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Yes, please—I'm starving.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm hungrier than you.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You're always hungry, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Because I'm strong.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Strong at eating, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yesterday felt good. Really good.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It did. You boys did solid work.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And nobody got hurt. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: When's the first snow, do you think?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Few weeks yet. We'll see signs first.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We'll need more firewood before then.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We will. But today, we just rest.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I help carry wood later?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After lessons, maybe. For now, eat.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good morning, all. Really good morning.

action: stands back from the cabin to study the roof line, nodding at its solid angle, then settles on the porch with a cup of coffee to keep an eye on the boys.
thought: That roof will hold the winter.

action: spreads the homeschool books across a bench on the porch, settling the boys with arithmetic problems while she keeps the midday meal simmering in the stove.
thought: Rest day. They've earned it. We all have.

action: works through his math lessons at the porch bench, pencil steady, glancing up now and then at the roof his own hands helped hold.
thought: We built that. We really built it.

action: sits restless at the bench, fidgeting through fractions, eyes drifting toward the creek where he swears the salmon are jumping.
thought: Can we fish? Can we fish yet?

action: sprawls on the porch rug with his letters, playing with the shapes while half-listening to Maggie explain addition to the bigger boys.
thought: Warm porch, warm stove. Safe and quiet.

description: Lessons stretch into quiet midday on the porch—everyone fed, everyone steady, the roof's hold giving permission to simply be together.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Sawyer, you're up. Fractions on the board.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Three-quarters of twenty is fifteen, right?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Exactly. Finn, you next?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Um. Half of sixteen?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eight. Good. Bear, what's two plus three?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Five! I got it!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You did. We're making real progress.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Roof didn't leak once last night. That's good building.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We all did that together, though. Every one of us.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's right. You all did.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Dad, can we fish after school? Please?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finish your lessons first. Then we'll see.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Mom always says 'we'll see.' That means no.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It means 'if you finish your work, maybe yes.'

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I like this better than building, actually.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: What's 'this,' buddy?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Everyone here. No one worried. Just... quiet.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Me too. We needed quiet.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The work earned us that. The real work earns rest.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: What's next? After the roof is... done?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Winterize. Seal cracks. The woodshed, if we can.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One project at a time. Right now, school.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Then fishing?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Then we'll talk about fishing.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I finished my letters!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Show me. Very good, Bear.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That roof was worth the work, though.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It was. We're going to make it through winter.

action: Spends the afternoon stacking firewood with Sawyer, teaching him how to arrange it so the wood seasons properly through the fall.
thought: That roof won't let us down now.

action: Keeps the cabin warm and bread rising, then settles on the porch watching the boys work and play, content in the ease of the day.
thought: This rest is what we're building toward.

action: Helps his dad organize and stack the firewood with care, learning how to arrange it tight to the outside for proper seasoning.
thought: I'm actually getting how this works.

action: Finally drags Bear to the creek and spends the afternoon fishing in the clear water, catching his first real fish of the season.
thought: I actually caught one. Actually caught one!

action: Follows Finn to the creek and explores around the rocks, poking for crayfish and watching his brother fish, content to be part of the day.
thought: Finn finds the best places to explore.

description: With the roof secure and the day clear, Cole and Sawyer work the firewood stack while Maggie keeps the cabin warm and Finn finally gets his wish to fish at the creek with Bear.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That roof held strong. We did good work.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Everyone earned a quieter day after that push.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Should I organize this stack or cut more?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Organize. We've got plenty cut. Just needs stacking right.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can Bear and I go to the creek, Dad?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Stay out of the deep parts. You know the rule.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: We know! Finn says the fish are real close today.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Go on. Just check in before dinner.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Is this how you want it? Tight on the outside?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Exactly. Air moves through the middle and dries it faster.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: How much more do we need before winter?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Another cord, maybe. We've got time while it's clear.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Finn! There's a crayfish under that rock!

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Don't grab it—they pinch. Just look.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: It's neat! Can we keep it?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: No, it lives here. Come on, there's a fishing spot—

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Dad, why does the wood season? I don't get it.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Wet wood doesn't burn hot. Seasoning lets the water out.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long does that take?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Months. So we cut in summer, stack in fall, burn in winter.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Fish! I got one! Actually got one!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: That's huge! It's huge, Finn!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's wonderful!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Bring it here when you're done. That's dinner.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Really? I caught dinner?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Finn caught dinner! We're the hunter guys!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That's how it works. You fish, you eat.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Honest work pays back, every time.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come on up when you're tired. I've got bread ready.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: And Finn can learn to clean that fish.

action: Settles onto the cabin porch as evening cools, watching the day's work hold.
thought: This roof will hold the winter.

action: Brings warm plates to the porch, calling the family in to rest and eat.
thought: We've earned this quiet night together.

action: Helps settle the meal, moving with quiet confidence from the day's hard work.
thought: We actually built that roof ourselves.

action: Bounces onto the porch, still buzzed from the day's fishing, too happy to sit still yet.
thought: Today was absolutely perfect for everything.

action: Follows Finn to the porch, already planning tomorrow's adventures while the stove glows warm inside.
thought: This is the best place ever.

description: As the cool evening settles, the family gathers on the cabin porch—the roof finally secure, the stove glowing inside, and for the first time since work began, there's room to simply sit together and rest.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Roof held strong all day. That's going to matter come January.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It will. You all earned a real rest tonight.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We actually finished it. I still can't believe it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: And I caught a fish! Remember? I actually caught one!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Finn showed me how to spot the deep spots in the creek.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Then tomorrow you can teach us both, Finn.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Dinner's still warm. Let's eat while the stove's hot.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: You used the venison again?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Last of it. We'll restock from the freezer tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we have seconds?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: The stove kept everything so warm today, even outside.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That roof will keep the heat in when fall really hits.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We're ready for it now. That's what matters.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Better than we were two months ago.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Way better. Remember when there were just walls and sky?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: When we first got here there was nothing but dirt.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: And now look—a home. A real home.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Our home. Eat, boys, before it cools.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: This is really good, Mom.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The best. It's the best.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we sit and watch the stars after?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: If you don't all fall asleep first.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Unlikely after a day like that.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Worth every minute though.

action: After a final check of the cabin, Cole settles on the porch with Maggie to watch the aurora dance across the clear fall sky.
thought: This roof will hold the winter.

action: With Finn's fish prepared and the family gathered, Maggie settles on the porch with a cup of warm tea, watching the sky clear into aurora.
thought: They're warm, they're fed, we're safe.

action: Sawyer leans against the cabin wall, tired from the day's work but pleased with the roof, watching the aurora begin to shimmer green.
thought: We built something real and it holds.

action: Finn sits on the porch steps, full from his own catch and beaming as the aurora starts to light the sky above the cabin.
thought: I caught one. I'm part of this.

action: Bear nestles against Maggie's side on the porch, fighting back yawns as the first green light traces the fall sky.
thought: This is the best place ever.

description: As Finn's first catch cooks for dinner and the aurora starts its green dance, the family gathers on the porch—the first moment of rest since the roof work began.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I can't believe I actually got one.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: You should've seen his face when it bit!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come help me get this ready to cook.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I cook it?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You can help. First you learn to clean it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: He's gonna be fishing every chance now.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the way it happens.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is the roof really done?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: As done as a roof gets in fall.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Took long enough.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Took what it took. You did good work.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The water was so cold.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And you both stayed warm anyway.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the skill, kid. Work hard, stay smart.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Will we catch more tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Maybe. The creek's good right now.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We have to check the woodpile first.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We do. But Finn's earned a morning off if he wants it.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Look at the sky. Is that it?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The lights! The lights are starting!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Clear enough tonight. We might see a show.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I've never seen the full aurora.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You will. All of you will.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: It's amazing every time.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come on, dinner first, then we watch.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we eat on the porch?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: If you don't freeze.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We won't. We'll be warm from the fish!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: There's the spirit.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Best meal of the week.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's because he caught it.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: That's why it tastes better.

action: Cole stands at the porch edge with morning coffee, surveying the finished roof line as the cool autumn air clears his head.
thought: Roof will hold. Now for the next priority.

action: Maggie moves between the breakfast setup and the schoolwork table, keeping the boys fed and on task with the day's lessons.
thought: They need this rhythm. School, then work.

action: Sawyer sits at the school table with a plate of food, already thinking through the next build project and what materials they'll need.
thought: We did the hard part. What's next matters.

action: Finn eats quickly, barely able to sit still, already planning the next build and asking questions about the day ahead.
thought: Woodshed next—huge one. I'll help build it.

action: Bear sits close to his mom, eating slowly and watching the morning action, secure and content in the warm cabin with his family.
thought: This is the best. Warm food, everyone here.

description: The cabin is warm and the roof overhead is solid; Cole stands on the porch with coffee while Maggie herds the boys to the breakfast table and school lesson, and the family's energy is high—the roof is secure, and Cole's already thinking ahead to the next project before winter closes in.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come on, you three—breakfast is getting cold.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Roof looks solid. We did that right.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Three days of actual rain wouldn't bother it now.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: No, it wouldn't. You did real work up there.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we build a woodshed next? Something huge?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I want to help carry the big logs.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: School first, builders second. Math on the table.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Woodshed's smart. We'll talk it through after lessons.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We need materials though, right? And we've got—

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Forty dollars left. Yeah. We'll need a town run soon.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Not this week. Fuel's expensive and we've got food.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But the firewood—

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Firewood's fine. We're at ninety-four percent. We gather what we need.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: What about power? The battery's getting low.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Solar panels, eventually. For now, we keep the stove going and use daylight.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The cabin's already warm.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It is. And that's the stove, not much else.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll solve it. One thing at a time, and we start with school.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Then woodshed?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Then woodshed. Now eat.

thought: Power's down. Woodshed next, but town run first.

action: Wraps up the midday school lessons with the boys and transitions the family to lunch and planning mode as the afternoon work begins.
thought: Roof's done. Now what, and with what?

action: Listens to his parents' discussion of the power situation and immediately volunteers to help inventory materials and supplies for the woodshed build.
thought: If we're building it, I should know what we need.

action: Bounces with energy as the woodshed is mentioned and peppers Cole with questions about the size and scope of the next big build.
thought: Woodshed next? I'm framing it all!

action: Declares he wants to help with the woodshed and sticks close to Finn, ready to tag along wherever the day takes the family next.
thought: I'm helping with the big woodshed!

description: As Cole discovers the solar is nearly depleted at 6%, the family gathers at the cabin to plan tomorrow's fuel run and the woodshed that waits beyond.

dialogue.line: Solar's at six percent. We need a fuel run tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Makes sense. How's the cabin temp?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Still good. The stove's holding fine.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: So... what's next? The woodshed?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Yeah. But we need materials first.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And more food. We're running low.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer, after lunch let's do a full count.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: What are we counting?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Everything. Materials, tools, what we're short on.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: So we know what to buy in town.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How big's the woodshed going to be?

dialogue.line: Maybe sixteen by twenty, if the lumber's right.

dialogue.line: That's HUGE. I'm totally framing it.

dialogue.line: I want to help build it too!

dialogue.line: We'll all help. One step at a time.

dialogue.line: First, lunch. Fire or table?

dialogue.line: Fire. It's a good day for it.

dialogue.line: We can talk through the inventory while we eat.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Good thinking. Come on, boys.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: This woodshed's gonna be epic.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The best ever!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Let's make it so. Come on.

action: He stands at the cabin porch with coffee, mentally tallying what town needs: fuel, maybe bolt stock if money stretches, and eyes the truck for tomorrow's early run.
thought: Six percent. Early start, long list, tight money.

action: She sets hot food on the table and gathers the family inside to eat warm and plan the fuel run, settling the evening with care and purpose.
thought: They're tired. Food and plans and early sleep.

action: He eats at the table, quiet and thoughtful, absorbing Cole's plan for tomorrow while thinking ahead to the woodshed frame.
thought: Roof's done. Shed's next. I can frame that.

action: He bounces slightly in his seat, rapid-fire about the woodshed dimensions and eagerly pressing when they start building.
thought: Tomorrow we start. Big one. I can help.

action: He sits warm by the table, eating steadily and contentedly, watching the older ones talk and plan while the evening cools outside.
thought: Warm cabin. Belly full. Everyone here.

description: As evening cools and clears, the family gathers warm at the cabin with hot dinner, Cole sketching tomorrow's fuel run while Finn bounces about the woodshed and everyone settles into plans and warmth.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Hot food. Everyone inside while it's warm.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fuel run at dawn. We're down to six percent.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But we're starting the woodshed after, right? Right?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long are you gone, Dad?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Few hours. Fuel, maybe some bolt stock if money stretches.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It won't stretch far. Sixty dollars left.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: That's not even—can we still build it?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Firewood matters more than the shed.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One thing at a time. Fuel first, then we see.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is the truck cold in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Probably. But she'll start.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat while it's hot. We'll make a list tonight.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can help organize what we need.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But how big is the shed roof going to be?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One roof at a time, bud.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: The cabin roof is done. That's the win tonight.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The cabin's warm now. That's really good.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It is. That roof is solid. We did good.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The real test is winter.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One season at a time, same as projects.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help load the truck tonight for tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: After dinner. We'll get the fuel cans ready.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: What if the generator won't start in the cold?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It'll start. We're not running it until we're back.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Tonight we eat, plan, and rest. Early run tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I come with you, Dad?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Not this time, buddy. Too cold and too long.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Okay.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: So after you get back, we really start building?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Let's worry about tomorrow after today is done.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: And after coffee.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Always after coffee.

action: Cole sketches the fuel run by lamplight, reviewing every detail while hot stew steams and the family gathers around him.
thought: Five-thirty. Clear skies. We can do this.

action: Maggie ladles hot stew and settles the family warm at the table, keeping the evening orderly and full of quiet care.
thought: Keep them warm and ready for five-thirty.

action: Sawyer helps with stew and listens close to Cole's plans, proud to be asked to help on the truck run tomorrow.
thought: Woodshed framing from scratch. I can design this.

action: Finn bounces on the bench between bites, peppering Cole with framing angles and measurements despite the late hour.
thought: All the pieces, angles, measurements. So clear.

action: Bear eats slowly, yawns, and nestles against Maggie as the warm cabin and full belly pull him toward sleep.
thought: Warm. Full. Everyone here. The best night yet.

description: Night falls clear and cool; the family gathers warm at the cabin—Cole reviewing the fuel run by lamplight, Sawyer listening close, Finn bouncing with woodshed talk, Maggie settling Bear inside toward sleep as the first aurora shimmers above the treeline.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Hot stew, everyone. Eat while it's warm.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fuel run at five-thirty. Long day ahead.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can help. Do I come with you?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Yeah, son. You and me. Your mom stays with the boys.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Okay. I've done it before, but—yeah.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But what about the woodshed? Don't we start tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After you eat, Finn. Stew first, plans second.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Woodshed frames next. Sawyer can help design it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Really? From scratch?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You've helped frame the roof. You know the angles.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I know the angles too! I can measure—

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Mmm.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat up, little man. Big day tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: All of us. Town haul, then back to build.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How many pieces? Like, exactly how many?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll count them as we cut, remember?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The power's at five percent. That's urgent.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It is. That's why we're up at five.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Oh, look. The lights.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Clear skies holding. Good for tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is that the aurora? The green ones?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: First real show of the year.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Clear skies, clear roads. We'll make good time.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Let's get these two to bed.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good rest tonight. Early morning waiting.

action: stokes the wood stove at pre-dawn, then moves to the truck to load empty fuel cans and check the route one last time.
thought: Clear roads. We can do this.

action: puts hot breakfast on the table, then steps outside to watch the boys load the truck and waves them away.
thought: Five hours. They'll be back by noon.

action: helps Cole secure the fuel cans in the truck bed, checking each tie-down twice the way his father taught him.
thought: This matters. I'll do it right.

action: bounces between helping load the cans and asking a dozen questions about the route, the town, and what they'll find there.
thought: We're going to town! Finally, finally!

action: eats oatmeal by the warm stove, watches the truck being loaded, then climbs into Maggie's lap with a sigh.
thought: I want to go too, so bad.

description: Cole and the boys load the truck for town while Maggie and Bear watch from the cabin, breakfast cleared and the day split between the road and a quiet homeschool morning.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Cans are loaded. Roads are clear. We're good.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Map says ninety minutes if we take the ridge cut.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is the ridge cut open this time of year?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Should be. We'll check on the radio first.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Hot breakfast is inside if anyone's hungry before you go.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I come?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're with me today, buddy. Math and firewood.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Firewood's not as fun as town.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We'll bring back something good, Bear.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we get candy?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fuel first. Extras after.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Bundle up, all three. It's cold.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Already planned. We've got layers.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I have the list—fuel, parts, hinges, nails.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: And the axe handle!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Don't forget the axe handle!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Already written. We're not forgetting anything.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Drive safe. If ice, take it slow.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Always.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Truck's running. We're good?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We're good. Let's move.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Let's go, let's go!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Five hours. We'll see you at lunch.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Maybe sooner if town's quick.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Bring something cool!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You got it, bud.

action: Maps out the woodshed foundation on the cleared build site, measuring post spacing against the timber they've got on hand and the winter winds ahead.
thought: Clear day. Push the framing hard while we can.

action: Wraps up midday lessons with the younger boys, then sets out lunch at the cabin table—bread, cheese, and tea—before heading out to check on Cole's progress.
thought: Fuel them well. Afternoon's the real push.

action: Stands with Cole at the build site, studying the post layout, asking questions about load-bearing and angles, his notebook already filling with sketches.
thought: Dad trusts me with this design work.

action: Bolts through his last math problem, then heads toward the build site, eager to help with anything that looks like real work.
thought: Building starts today. I'm gonna help.

action: Finishes his letters practice while sitting with Maggie, then helps her gather lunch things, staying close to her as she moves in and out of the cabin.
thought: Everyone's working on something big today.

description: Cole maps the woodshed on a clear fall afternoon while Maggie sets out lunch and the boys crowd around the table and build site, all of them tuned to the work ahead.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Posts here and here—that's the main load-bearing frame.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Won't the wind push hardest on the north face?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Exactly. That's why we're going deep on those posts.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat first, you lot. Bread and cheese, come on.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we cut the posts today?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Need to mark the trees first. Make sure they're straight.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer's right. Good timber takes time to pick.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: What's my job? Can I help with something?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You can help me carry posts when we're ready, okay?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Really? I'm strong enough?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're strong enough. Come sit and eat first.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The goal is to have framing up before the first hard freeze.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How long does that usually take?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Three weeks, maybe four if the weather turns bad.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We've got eight days of good weather left this season.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Then we work steady every clear day.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'm not tired. Let's start this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Timber'll be wet if we cut today. Better to wait till it dries.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Or we mark the trees and fell them tomorrow, let them sit a day.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Fell them? Like knock them down?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: With the chainsaw! That's gonna be so loud.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat your lunch. And yes, very loud.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, you and Bear can watch from a safe spot.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can Sawyer work the chainsaw?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Not yet. Dad's teaching me the safety rules first.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One step at a time. You've got time to learn.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: This is turning into a real build. The woodshed will be solid.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It'll stand fifty years if we do this right.

action: Spent the afternoon mapping the woodshed site with Sawyer, marking out the footprint and checking sight lines for a winter-long store of firewood.
thought: Generator's almost empty. Fuel run soon.

action: Worked through afternoon lessons with the boys at the table, then started prepping dinner as Cole and Sawyer returned from the site.
thought: Food's running low. Gotta stretch it smart.

action: Worked alongside Cole on the woodshed design, asking questions about depth and roof angle, growing more confident in the real responsibility.
thought: I can actually do this design work.

action: Finished his math lesson at the table, restless and eager, then lingered near Maggie and Cole, asking questions about the woodshed and dinner.
thought: Can I help design stuff tomorrow? Please?

action: Worked through schoolwork, then sat with Maggie as bread and tea came out, watching the older boys and asking about helping with the big build.
thought: I want to help stack firewood so bad.

description: Cole and Sawyer returned from mapping the woodshed site as Maggie called everyone in for bread and tea, the family gathering at the porch as the afternoon wound toward dinner.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Posts'll go here and here—good wind protection from the trees.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yeah, and if the roof angles south, we get more light in winter.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You two bring those plans inside soon! Tea's ready.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: In a minute—Sawyer, what d'you think about depth?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Maybe twelve feet? Enough for a whole winter stacked high.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is that bigger than our cabin?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Focus on your math, sweetie. Cole, come eat.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I want to help stack it when we build!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You bet you will. Let me just wash up.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Just bread and jam. Better than nothing after a day like this.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: After site work, even bread sounds amazing.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Clear day like this, you gotta push hard. Winter's not far.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Tell me about it. Already thinking root storage and meat.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we have soup for dinner? With cheese?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: If we keep the stove hot and use the vegetables well.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Woodpile's at ninety—we're solid on that front.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Once the shed's up, we'll keep it all dry for months.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: And it keeps the bears away?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Not really, buddy. But it keeps OUR wood safe and dry.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Finish that bread, then get your hands washed. Dinner in an hour.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help measure the site tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Absolutely. Fresh eyes help a lot.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Just don't mess up my dimensions, okay?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'll be careful. Mostly.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's what scares me.

action: Settled at the warming firepit with the family after a day of framing, the clear sky and fire drawing them close for an evening meal.
thought: Clear nights like this are gift time.

action: Brought out a simple dinner to the warming firepit where the family gathered, settling with Cole and the boys to share the meal and evening.
thought: Food stretched. Everyone warm and full.

action: Came to the firepit with Dad and the boys after the day's framing work, hungry and proud, settling by the warmth to eat and watch the sky.
thought: That wall is coming up solid.

action: Bounded out to the firepit where the family was gathering, eager for dinner and even more eager to stay up and watch for the aurora lights.
thought: I hope we see the lights tonight.

action: Followed everyone out to the firepit, drawn to the warmth of the fire and the family gathered close, settling in for dinner and the promise of evening.
thought: Everyone's here. The sky's so clear.

dialogue.line: Generator's still quiet. Fuel run's coming up.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Day or two if this weather holds.

dialogue.line: Let's stretch what we've got tonight.

dialogue.line: When do we go in? Soon as possible?

dialogue.line: Weather's clear. Two, three days maybe.

dialogue.line: Can we get more food at once?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We can try, sparks. We'll see.

dialogue.line: Sky like this won't last, but it's good now.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Long enough to push the framing forward.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You're coming into your own with that work, Saw.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I learned from the best.

dialogue.line: Can I help more with the building tomorrow?

dialogue.line: You already are, sparks. All afternoon.

dialogue.line: But tomorrow I want to help design—

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Finn, eat. Mouth full, no talking.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Okay okay okay.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we see the lights tonight?

dialogue.line: If we're lucky, buddy. Sky's clear enough.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we stay up and watch?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: A little bit. Not too late.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: To remember a day like this.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: To remember we're getting it right.

action: Cole tended the fire, adding wood to hold the heat through the long night, eyes on the darkening treeline.
thought: This night holds more than just the cold.

action: Maggie settled beside Cole with a thermos of tea, warm hands wrapped around it, watching the boys' faces by firelight.
thought: Moments like these are why we came here.

action: Sawyer sprawled on a blanket, eyes tracing the dark sky above the treeline, one hand gesturing as he talked.
thought: Could actually see something beautiful tonight.

action: Finn bounced between sitting and standing, scanning the northern horizon with the kind of focus he brought to everything.
thought: What if the lights come? What if they do?

action: Bear nestled against his mother, cozy and drowsy as the fire crackled, occasionally asking quiet questions about the sky.
thought: I'm warm. Everyone's here. It's perfect.

description: A clear autumn night draws the family to the firepit, eyes on the sky and hope in the air—Finn's whisper about the lights from yesterday now shared by all, watching together as the dark deepens.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Night like this is a gift—clear all the way up.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Do you think we'll actually see the lights tonight?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Could be. Clear skies, cold snap coming in. Perfect timing.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: What color will they be? Are they green?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Green mostly. Sometimes purple or deep red. You have to be patient.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The wall came together solid today. Another week and that corner's done.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Sawyer, can I really help with the design tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yeah. Grab the notebook after breakfast. I'll show you the layout.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Food's getting tight, but everyone's warm and full tonight. That matters.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is winter coming? Like... really soon?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Few more weeks of fall. But fuel's almost gone. Town run soon.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Wednesday maybe, if the weather holds. I'll write a list.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: After the wall, the woodshed next, right? That's the priority?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Exactly. Materials are ready. Storm-proof storage before the first snow.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help saw and stack the wood?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Me too! I want to help stack so bad!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You both will. That's how this place gets built—all hands.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: For now, just breathe. The work will be there tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The cabin's warmer every week. That stove's really working.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Wait—is that a glow? On the north side?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Where? Where? I don't see it!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Keep watching. They'll come if they want to show themselves.

action: Cole gathers his framing tools and heads to the build site before the morning light dims, energized and clear-headed about the day's work.
thought: Frame first, fuel after. Get this up today.

action: Maggie stretches out breakfast for all five from yesterday's stores, rationing carefully, then settles at the porch with a mug of coffee and the day's plan.
thought: Food's tightening. Fuel run has to happen.

action: Sawyer eats quickly and follows his dad to the build site, eager to learn the framing work and prove he can handle a real structural piece.
thought: Dad's teaching me this. I can do it.

action: Finn bolts his breakfast down and races after Cole and Sawyer to the build site, already asking a dozen questions about the frame and what comes next.
thought: Real frame work today. I'm so ready.

action: Bear sits close by Maggie on the porch, warming his hands on her coffee mug and asking if he can help with the food or the day's tasks.
thought: Mom's here. Warm. What can I do?

description: Cole and the boys raise the first frame section together, the structure taking shape as morning spreads across the build site and the real work begins.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer, keep that corner steady. Finn, watch where the joints sit.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Got it. This one fits tight.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is this going to be the whole wall?

dialogue.line: First section. Then the next piece. Like we planned.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long do you think framing takes?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: On good days, couple cycles if we keep moving and materials hold.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Then we do the roof, right?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Not today, buddy. One thing at a time.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn's got the long view, though. That's good thinking.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: The roof matters. Cold will come.

dialogue.line: It will. So this frame has to be solid first.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Is this the last on-site material we've got?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: For now. Your mom and I are talking about a town run this afternoon for more.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Town? Today?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Fuel and materials, probably. Power's running low.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You two stay here with the frame. I'll come back after the run.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But you're teaching us.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: I'm teaching you NOW. Watch how this sets. You'll know what comes next.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We can do the next section if you mark it.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Mark it after lunch. Maggie's got school for you two first.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: School? We're framing.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Both, I think. One after the other.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Home isn't just building. It's knowing things too.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Math and the frame—same thing though, right?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Pretty close, yeah.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Exactly. Alright, watch. I'm going to show you how the next angle works.

action: Walks the marked posts with Sawyer and Finn, checking angles and laying out the next frame section's route.
thought: Steady work, steady pace. The land responds well.

action: Dishes out a warm, modest midday meal at the cabin porch, Bear close by helping with the serving.
thought: Stretch it, keep it warm. That's my job.

action: Stands with Cole at the frame site, checking angles and taking careful measurements for the vertical posts.
thought: Dad trusts me with this now.

action: Keeps the saw blade sharp and the cutting marks clear, bouncing on his toes, ready to start.
thought: Real building. This is what I came for.

action: Helps Maggie carry dishes and bread to the porch table, eager to feed the builders coming in soon.
thought: I'm helping Mom keep the big guys fed.

description: Cole and his sons mark and measure the frame posts at the build site, reading angles and planning the week's work in the clear fall air.

dialogue.line: Alright. This corner post goes flush with the line. See?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Like the section we raised yesterday.

dialogue.line: Exactly. You're reading the angles right.
